stem.en: Renu says that all parts of a plant, even roots, contain plastids. Rohit says roots have no plastids, because roots are underground and do not make food. Who is correct?

text.en: Rohit, because every plastid is a green chloroplast.

feedback.en: Chromoplasts and leucoplasts are plastids too, and they are not green.

text.en: Renu, because roots have colourless plastids that store food.

feedback.en: Yes. Leucoplasts need no light, because they store food and do not make it.

text.en: Rohit, because plastids can form only in parts that get light.

feedback.en: Potato and taro store starch in plastids, under the ground.

text.en: Neither, because plastids are found only in flowers and fruits.

feedback.en: Leaves have chloroplasts, so plastids are not found only there.

explanation.en: Rohit is thinking only of chloroplasts. Leucoplasts are plastids as well, and they store food, so roots can have them without any light.

hints.en: Is every plastid used for making food?
